notes: 32 of the 80 local photos opened and read visually; all 80 additionally measured programmatically (non-white bounding box + row/column silhouette profiles) to check published aspect ratios. The remote CDN filenames recorded in data/brands.json name the view and the variant for every local file (e.g. '..._1_challenge_0_5L_dark_tan_bike_bags_front.jpg'), so each local -1..-4 could be mapped to a known view/size before measuring. Brooks' own spec tables label three numbers Height / Length / Width but do not apply those labels consistently between models, so every dims_raw below quotes the table verbatim and dims_note says which physical axis each number was assigned to and what evidence settled it.

brand_construction.leather_billet_attachment: The Classic bags (Challenge, D-Shaped) hang from the saddle's bag loops on vegetable-tanned leather BILLETS, not webbing. A billet is a plain leather tongue about 12-15 mm wide and 2.5-3 mm thick with a single line of round punched holes down its length. Each billet is riveted or stitched to the bag and passes upward through a polished nickel-plated STEEL ROLLER BUCKLE - a rectangular frame with a centre bar carrying a free-spinning brass/steel roller and a single tapered tongue that drops into a punched hole. Above every roller buckle sits a second plain rectangular keeper loop (no tongue) that the billet tail is tucked back through, so the tail lies flat against the bag and points DOWN. There is no ladderlock, no cam and no side-release buckle anywhere on the heritage line. On the Trekking line (Isle of Wight, Rambler, Haul) the same idea is executed in black leather/Hypalon strapping with polished steel dome rivets instead of stitching, over a waxed cotton body. Anything rendered with nylon webbing and a plastic side-release buckle is the Scape line, not the heritage line.
brand_construction.hardware_finish: Classic + Trekking: polished nickel/steel, warm grey-white highlights (#c9ccce), no black plastic. Scape: silver anodised aluminium cam buckles (#c9c9c9) plus matte black acetal cam and ladderlock hardware.

materials.Classic: vegetable-tanned leather throughout, body and straps the same hide and colour
materials.Trekking: weather-resistant waxed cotton / waxed canvas body (Seal Brown) with BLACK leather and Hypalon strapping - body colour and strap colour differ
materials.Commuting: water-resistant cotton canvas body with glossy black vegetable-tanned leather trim and billet
materials.Scape: coated woven nylon / TPU-laminated fabric, Hypalon details, nylon webbing, aluminium hardware

products.name: Seat Bag
products.dims_raw: Height 180 mm / Length 140 mm / Width 400-600 mm / Capacity 8 L / Max load 3 kg / Weight 500 g
products.dims_note: CHANGED under the unfurled rule (was 46). The 400-600 mm range is the roll travel and it runs along the bag's own length, nose to tail - photo -3 shows the roll bundle at the tail and the long holster tongue running forward to the saddle. Unfurled length is therefore the 600 mm MAX = 60 cm. Height 180 and depth 140 are single published figures, so they are already at minimum. 60 x 14 x 18 = 15.1 L box against an 8 L rating, which is expected: the unfurled plan extent is not the packed volume.

render.basis: SCHEMA NOTE: on this product the variable axis is the LENGTH, not the height - the roll runs nose-to-tail, so len_cm carries the render correction and hgt_cm simply restates the fixed published 180 mm. Brooks publishes the roll travel as a 400-600 mm range, so the drawn length takes the 400 mm MINIMUM. Photo scape-seat-bag-8l-3.jpg (top view) shows the tail turned down about three times, consistent with the short end of that range. Drawing the 60 cm unfurled figure would put the tail into the rear tyre.
render.note: hgt_cm is fixed, not a correction; len_cm is the field that matters here

geometry.notes: Holster-and-drybag, not a single sewn bag. The holster has a long narrow triangular TONGUE at the nose that runs forward under the saddle and carries the rail straps - it is only a few cm deep and is not a load-carrying part of the volume. The body swells rearward from that tongue to a full-depth blunt tail where the drybag rolls down. So unlike most seat packs the fat end is at the BACK. Bottom face carries a black textured abrasion 'mudguard' panel.

closure.hardware: roll folds down and a webbing strap running forward along the top face pulls it to a silver anodised aluminium cam buckle on the holster spine

details.valve: round black air-release valve on the side panel, mid-body, to purge the drybag
details.lightMount: webbing light loop at the tail
details.fabric: matte TPU-laminated shell over a removable IPX4 drybag; abrasion panel on the underside

mount.notes: Tongue clamps flat between the saddle rails; the body cantilevers rearward and the tail is the heaviest part, so it droops. Roll the tail down before checking tyre clearance.

products.name: Saddle Roll Bag
products.dims_raw: Height 100 mm / Length 100 mm / Width 320 mm / Capacity 1 L / Weight 75 g
products.dims_note: CHANGED under the unfurled rule (was 18.6). 320 mm against a 100 x 100 mm cross-section would be 3.2 L, so 320 is the FLAT/UNFURLED length, not the packed length - and the rule now asks for the unfurled figure, so len = 32. The 100 mm cross-section figures are single values and stand as the minimum. See the render block for the packed length actually to be drawn.

render.basis: SCHEMA NOTE: the variable axis here is the LENGTH, not the height - len_cm carries the render correction and hgt_cm restates the fixed published 100 mm cross-section. Brooks publishes only the 320 mm UNFURLED length and no range, so the packed length is measured from photographs of the packed article: scape-saddle-roll-bag-1l-1.jpg (right side) and -3.jpg (left side). The bag lies diagonally in frame, so I took the principal axis of the mud-green body by PCA on the colour mask. Both views agree - long axis to maximum belly thickness is 2.74 and 2.64, call it 2.6. Against Brooks' 100 mm belly that gives a packed length of about 26 cm, and a tapered crescent 26 cm long on a 10 cm belly comes out at roughly 1 L, matching the rating. These are studio shots, not on-bike shots - Brooks published no on-bike image of this bag in the set that was downloaded.
render.note: hgt_cm is fixed, not a correction; len_cm is the field that matters here

geometry.notes: A flat sleeve rolled from BOTH ends toward the middle, so packed it reads as a crescent: fat oval belly, tapering to two flattened rolled-down ends. Ends do not stay round.

closure.hardware: both ends roll inward and clip to a matte black acetal cam buckle on the belly strap

details.fabric: coated woven nylon, matte, fine visible weave

mount.notes: Hangs directly under the saddle with its long axis ACROSS the bike (rail to rail), not fore-aft - the two hook-and-loop tabs on the top face wrap the two rails and the webbing strap drops forward to the seatpost. Do not render it pointing at the rear wheel.

products.name: Isle of Wight Saddle Bag
products.dims_raw: Height 110 mm / Length 210 mm / Width 130 mm / Capacity 2 L / Weight 200 g
products.dims_note: Confirmed by photo. Local -3 is the plan (top) view and local -4 the underside; both are flat-on and measure 1.67-1.73 long-to-wide, against a published 210/130 = 1.62. That directly confirms 210 as the fore-aft length and 130 as the across-the-bike width, with 110 the height. 21 x 13 x 11 = 3.0 L box for a 2 L rating - reasonable given how strongly the plan tapers.

geometry.notes: In PLAN it is a teardrop: a narrow rounded nose pointing forward that swells out to a broad, almost circular tail. In side elevation it is a fat rounded loaf with no flat faces at all. This is the only Brooks bag in the catalogue with a genuinely curved plan - do not model it as a box.

closure.hardware: two coated zips with black leather pull tabs

zips.notes: one zip runs down each side from the nose to the tail; opening both frees the whole upper panel, which lifts back as a hinged lid (photo -2 shows it peeled open, revealing a dark leather-lined interior). Both sliders park at the tail, tabs hanging down.

straps.notes: a single black leather strap about 15 mm wide crossing the bag TRANSVERSELY over the top, roughly two-thirds of the way back, and buckling to a small polished steel buckle on each side. Two polished steel dome rivets sit on the strap either side of the centreline. This is the piece that carries the whole bag.
black elastic shock cord with a barrel cord lock, emerging from a black Hypalon reinforcement patch at the nose and running forward/down to the seatpost

products.name: Rambler Handlebar Bag
products.dims_raw: Height 300 mm / Length 180 mm / Width 210 mm / Capacity 10 L / Weight 900 g
products.dims_note: REAL ERROR corrected - the axes were transposed. The old record read len 21 / hgt 30, i.e. a bag half a metre tall and narrow, standing on end. Photos -1 (front) and -3 (back) are both straight-on elevations and are unambiguously WIDER THAN TALL (bounding box 1.54, body-only 1.20). So Brooks' 300 mm is the across-the-bars run, not the height. The remaining two numbers are assigned 210 = height and 180 = fore-aft depth, which is what the side view (-2, 0.75 depth-to-height) supports and what makes a classic 10 L rando box: 30 x 21 x 18 = 11.3 L against 10 L stated, ratio 1.13. Medium rather than high because the 210/180 split between height and depth rests on the side-view ratio, and the flap standing proud inflates the measured height by 10-15%.

geometry.notes: Classic rando box, wider than tall, with a generous waxed-cotton flap that folds over the top and hangs down the front to about a third of the face. The flap's lower edge is a distinct dark horizontal band across the bag. Big black mesh drawcord pockets on both end panels stand proud of the body silhouette - they widen the bag noticeably in a front view and should be modelled as separate volumes, not as flat panels.

closure.hardware: two brown nylon webbing straps running vertically over the flap and down the front face to alloy/plastic hardware at the bottom; adjustable so no fabric is left flapping when the bag is under-filled

products.name: Haul Pannier
products.dims_raw: Height 370 mm / Length 130 mm / Width 330 mm / Capacity 22 L / Max load 7 kg / Weight 900 g. Brooks' 130 mm 'Length' is the flat body panel, not the loaded depth.
products.dims_note: Confirms and refines the previous pass. Photo -1 (front) measures 501 x 563 px on the body = 0.890, against a published 330/370 = 0.892 - so len 33 and hgt 37 are right and the image scale is 0.659 mm/px. Photo -2 (side) then gives a loaded depth of 290-306 px = 19.1-20.2 cm, not the 13 cm printed: the body is a rounded box and a full-height mesh pocket stands proud of each end, none of which is in Brooks' flat panel figure. wid kept at 20. 33 x 37 x 20 = 24.4 L against 22 L, ratio 1.11; the old 13 cm gave 15.9 L, less than the rating, which was impossible.

geometry.notes: Tall waxed-canvas box that narrows toward the bottom. Full-width flap over the top hanging a third of the way down the front. Black mesh drawcord pockets on both end panels standing clearly proud of the body - they are the widest thing on the bag in a front view.

closure.hardware: two brown webbing straps down the front face, each into a POLISHED ALLOY quick-release buckle - bright silver, not black plastic. They are the loudest hardware on the bag.

products.name: Half Haul Pannier
products.dims_raw: Height 370 mm / Length 160 mm / Width 210 mm / Capacity 12 L / Max load 7 kg / Weight 800 g
products.dims_note: len CHANGED from 21 to 27 on photographic evidence; hgt and wid left at Brooks' figures. Method: the Haul and Half Haul studio shots share a scale, proved by two identical physical parts measuring the same in both frames - the oval steel nameplate is 85 px on the Haul and 84 px on the Half Haul, and the white alloy buckle is 56x72 px vs 55x70 px. The Haul front view calibrates that scale at 0.659 mm/px (501 px = 330 mm). On the Half Haul the same measurement gives 560 px height = 369 mm, matching Brooks' printed 370 independently, and 411 px width = 271 mm, against Brooks' printed 210. Recorded as 27. This is a photo-over-table call, so confidence is medium; a reviewer can re-run it from the two front-view files. 27 x 37 x 16 = 16.0 L against 12 L, ratio 1.33 - higher than the Haul's 1.11, but the bag tapers hard toward the bottom and the mesh pockets are external.

geometry.notes: Same family as the Haul - a taller, narrower version of the same box, with the same flap, the same two-strap front and the same pair of end mesh pockets. Narrows more sharply toward the bottom than the Haul does.

products.name: Brick Lane Pannier
products.dims_raw: Height 360 mm / Length 120 mm / Width 350 mm / Capacity 15 L / Weight 950 g / Made in Italy. Fits racks 10-15 cm wide.
products.dims_note: Dimensions are PER SIDE, and the photos say so: local -1 is the outer face of ONE bag (remote name '..._bricklane_panniers_black_bike_bags_side.jpg') and measures 0.93 wide-to-tall against a published 350/360 = 0.97. Local -2 is the pair seen end-on ('..._front.jpg'); at that same scale the pair spans about 43 cm across, consistent with two 12 cm bodies plus a 10-15 cm rack between them. Note the item is SOLD as a joined pair draped over the rack - the two bags are permanently bridged by a canvas yoke - so a builder must place two of these, not one. The 15 L figure is ambiguous: 35 x 36 x 12 = 15.1 L is exactly one side's box, which suggests Brooks quotes 15 L per side, but the page does not say. Confidence medium on the capacity only; the geometry is solid.

geometry.notes: A flat, wide, almost square canvas slab with very little depth - it reads as a satchel, not a barrel. A large flap covers the top 55% of the outer face and finishes in a gently curved lower edge. Because the pair is joined by a yoke over the rack, the two bags share a single continuous top panel; render the bridge, not two independent bags. Photo -2 shows the pair splayed apart at the bottom with the yoke pinched in at the top.

closure.hardware: a single glossy black vegetable-tanned LEATHER billet running vertically down the centre of the flap onto the body, closed on a polished steel stud/snap - the only leather fastening on the Commuting line. Above it, the rolled top edge is laced across with black elastic cord through polished metal eyelets, which is what lets the bag roll down for volume.

straps.notes: centre of the flap, onto a steel stud
black elastic laced in a criss-cross through metal eyelets along the rolled top edge

logo.text: BROOKS / 18 ENGLAND 66 in warm gold on the flap, drive side of centre

details.fabric: water-resistant cotton canvas with vegetable-tanned leather finishing at the corners and edges

mount.notes: No hooks and no rail - the pair simply DRAPES over the rack top on its connecting yoke and is held by weight plus the elastic lacing; it releases when the tops are rolled. Needs a rear rack 10-15 cm wide. Because it hangs rather than clamps, it sits higher and further outboard than a hooked pannier.
